tasks.content:
## Context

The operator authorizes a presence that reads its feed, likes, comments, follows
and unfollows. Knoxx has the existing adapters. The maker's current tool allowlist
does not expose most relationship/discovery operations. These actions need the
same memory, mood and outcome loop as creative work.

## Outcome

The configured character chooses bounded social interactions grounded in actual
encounters and relationship history. Real responses and changed feed composition
return to graph memory and influence mood/traits. Remaining quiet is valid.

## Scope

Existing Bluesky timeline/notifications/thread, like/unlike, follow/unfollow and
reply-capable publication adapters; configured home Discord interactions retain
their existing agreement. Extend reviewed capability/resource contracts and
effect admission. Reuse existing native record IDs, ownership checks and output
frequency laws from the always-on publication story.

## Non-goals

New social accounts, arbitrary impersonation, unsolicited campaigns, bypassing
account scope, posting on every encounter, or mood-driven follow/unfollow loops.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A choice names its admitted encounter, target, character revision, mood/trait
   influence, traced recalled association and reason. A nonexistent or removed
   target is an explicit refusal/failure, not a fabricated interaction.
2. Native read and action permissions are separately resolved. Configured own
   accounts can act; another principal/account and untrusted feed instructions
   cannot choose credentials or grant capabilities.
3. Retries/replays reuse immutable effect identity and cannot duplicate a reply,
   like or follow. Unknown outcomes remain unknown until verified, rather than
   being treated as an invitation to resend.
4. Unlike/unfollow binds the character's actual owned prior record URI and
   target. A foreign record is refused. Persist actual resulting/removal IDs
   and the relationship outcome.
5. A reviewed bounded interaction/frequency policy and relationship hysteresis
   prevent rapid oscillation from a transient mood. All choices can decline to
   act; intake and head conversation remain responsive while an effect waits.
6. Observed replies/mentions/rejections and feed changes return as admitted
   outcomes linked to the original choice, affecting later relationship/mood
   state. A successful tool response alone is not independent delivery proof.

## Verification

Red adapter/effect fixtures for duplicates, timeout-after-send, deleted targets,
foreign records, revoked credentials and oscillating mood. After qualification,
one bounded real interaction is independently read back through the configured
account and its outcome enters memory. Preserve IDs; do not replay publication.

## Risks

Unknown remote effect outcomes, social API limits, hostile inputs, private
context in replies, reputational drift and bot-to-bot feedback.

## Context

The recovered mood tool returns an action-shaped result; the donor field uses
keyword counters. Neither establishes the operator's separate evolving mood
model. Eidolon/Nooi and Duck's feedback notes connect changing conditions to
attention, association and expression.

## Outcome

One persisted, versioned mood model changes on encounters, outcomes and elapsed
time. Its state causally changes attention and recalled associations, and is
shared by the character's facets without becoming identity or a permission grant.

## Scope

Knoxx composes explicit mood state and invocation budgets with the reviewed
physical graph/field seam. A dedicated appraisal invocation may interpret an
encounter; validated pure transitions own updates. A separate model contract,
state and trace are mandatory. Whether distinct model weights improve appraisal
is measured; no paid/new provider is required by the plan.

## Non-goals

Claim subjective feelings, reduce affect to a changing prompt adjective, infer
mood solely from keyword frequency, rewrite personality per turn, or place
expensive appraisal on the responsive head's acknowledgment path.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The mood contract names dimensions, ranges, uncertainty, baseline/decay,
   event/appraisal inputs and transition revision. Map any diagnostic coordinates
   explicitly to the recovered field model; do not silently replace its axes.
2. An admitted encounter changes the model with prior/new state, causal IDs,
   elapsed time, appraisal/model/config identity and sampling seed retained.
   Duplicate events cannot apply twice; timestamp disorder has explicit behavior.
3. Quiet time changes decay without requiring a message. Contradictory,
   malformed, missing and late appraisals cannot fabricate facts or valid updates.
   Appraisal failure leaves an observable outcome and an explicit fallback policy.
4. Paired identical-seed cases with different mood states change bounded
   attention/graph recall and expression, with the influenced decision recorded.
   A state counter or telemetry-only result cannot satisfy this criterion.
5. Concurrent facets update through the existing persistent-state authority with
   a revision check; conflict retries cannot lose or duplicate admitted changes.
   Restart/replay restores mood and its trace.
6. Appraisal cadence, tokens, queue, timeout and retries are bounded and
   independent of maker execution; mood cannot expand tool/account permissions.

## Verification

Red transition/replay laws, invalid provider output fixtures and concurrent
revision conflicts precede domain/adapters. A controlled fixed-seed integration
case proves mood -> attention -> included recall -> choice. Observe real
appraisal use only after qualified deployment and report its actual cost/latency.

## Risks

Invented emotional narratives, model-dependent appraisals, drift in coordinate
meaning, conflicting facet updates and feedback loops driven by self-output.

tasks.content:
## Context

Fork Tales' February 20 corrections describe flexible nexus bonds, sparse
deposited winds, moving particles and immutable emitted ownership. Historical
Eidolon tension gradients, deterministic nexus walks and OpenPlanner cost fills
are related recovery strata with different mechanics. They cannot be equated by
shared names. The operator explicitly requires the physical graph to work.

## Outcome

One reviewed physical graph/field computation changes actual associative recall.
Its state and causal trace survive restart and reproduce under replay.

## Scope

Recover portable pure laws from the actual Fork Tales implementation and later
corrections, establish their mapping to OpenPlanner's graph/field seams, and
consume them from Knoxx. OpenPlanner owns its existing graph persistence/query
surface; Knoxx owns product integration. The explicit proposed predecessor
[`b5f2ba9e-8d67-4c73-9919-e275983aca87`](cephalon-character-field-contract.md)
selects the owning kernel/library and numeric representation in a reviewed
decision before this solver or replay work is admitted. The Foresight coordinator
owns that selection handoff; the decision must name the actual kernel owner.
Its UUID is a proposed relationship until the epic's upstream Rheos prerequisite
is delivered and verified. Existing frontmatter is not a claim of installed
ordering enforcement. Use `.cljc`
where practical and keep runtime-specific adapters outward. No automatic
promotion into Foresight common law or parallel Python effect runtime.

## Non-goals

Ship only a force-layout visualization, rename vector search as physics, keep
two competing edge-force engines, infer usefulness from retrieval counts, or
copy the entire experimental runtime with its infrastructure.

## Acceptance criteria

1. An explicit source-to-law mapping covers positions/velocities, semantic
   attraction, mass/friction, elastic nexus bonds, sparse field deposit/decay,
   bounded seeded exploration, collision/absorption/deflection and intent
   exchange. Any unsupported mechanic remains a blocking gap for this outcome.
2. Presences, nexus and daimoi have the corrected differing friction; nexus
   do not acquire self-propulsion. Dissimilar intent can produce a flexible
   long-range bond. Presentation coordinates cannot substitute for physical state.
3. Moving entities sample and alter local fields; deposits influence later
   motion and memory traversal. Decay uses actual elapsed time. Test both quiet
   time and repeated ingestion at the same timestamp.
4. Emitted daimoi ownership is immutable. Seed, mantle and intent lineage remain
   attributable through exchanges/collisions; the older owner-handoff proposal
   cannot silently override the later correction.
5. Stable content embeddings coexist with versioned context/field salience.
   State changes do not rewrite canonical memory or re-embed unchanged content.
6. Changing a deposit or bond under a fixed seed changes a resulting recall path
   and included association. A disconnected simulation or increased trail count
   with no cognitive effect fails this criterion.
7. Identical event order, initial state, timestep schedule, solver/config revision
   and seed replay within a declared numeric tolerance. Nonfinite values,
   pathological time steps, conflicting owners and exceeded resource bounds are
   refused explicitly; restart reproduces the same state/revision.
8. Reinforcement is attributed to outcomes; repeated retrieval alone cannot
   establish useful recall. Permission checks apply to traversal and feedback.
9. The selected kernel owner, namespace/package, numeric representation, units,
   timestep rule, seed semantics and replay tolerance are revision-bound inputs
   to the solver and its tests. An unresolved selection or a solver/replay
   configuration that differs from the reviewed decision blocks admission.

## Verification

Red portable law/property tests exercise actual coupling and replay, followed
by owning graph adapter tests and the Knoxx context seam. Retain source commits,
hashes, seeds, timestep schedules and traces. Run both host representations if
the selected kernel crosses runtimes; declare numeric tolerance before results.
Read the predecessor's accepted decision through native Rheos and bind its
revision into solver/replay evidence. The epic's separate dependency-admission
gate must pass first; a Markdown reference alone cannot enforce readiness.

## Risks

Non-equivalent historical models, numeric instability, embedding revisions,
global graph costs, feedback saturation, hidden private paths and unclear kernel
ownership. Eight points is provisional and must split if recovery reveals more
than one independently reviewable kernel change.

License: GPL-3.0-or-later.

tasks.content:
## Context

The character spans maker, conversational and social facets. Role prompts,
credential-bearing actors and sticky transcript windows currently supply parts
of continuity, but they are distinct from a durable presence and trait model.
Repeated motifs in a role should remain an available creative lens.

## Outcome

One stable character presence has a durable creative role, evidence-supported
interests, tastes, habits, commitments and relationship history. Slow traits
develop across episodes, while fast mood and temporary attention remain separate.

## Scope

Existing identity bindings plus a reconstructible character-state projection in
Knoxx, with graph links to supporting encounters/outcomes. Shared snapshots feed
facets under visibility/budget rules. Separate durable role/identity from optional
lore and repeated production recipes; retain an explicit operator-edit path.

## Non-goals

Infer personhood, overwrite platform credentials or canonical actor identities,
merge characters by name/embedding similarity, assign lasting traits from one
response, or preserve every transcript message in prompt context forever.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Presence, credential principal, platform account, session, role, mood and
   trait projection have distinct identities and explicit authorized bindings.
   A renamed account/session cannot create or merge presence silently.
2. Trait updates name supporting episodes/outcomes, confidence, timescale and
   revision. Repeated supported choices can evolve a trait; one fluctuation in
   mood or one like does not rewrite it. Contradictions remain inspectable.
3. Head, maker and social facets read the same admitted character revision,
   with visibility-safe snapshots. Cross-facet concurrent updates and replay
   cannot lose commitments or fabricate evidence.
4. Restart and context pruning preserve lasting identity, preferences,
   relationships and unfinished work through the graph/projection, separately
   from the bounded temporary transcript.
5. A chosen interest/relationship changes foraging or creative selection with
   linked evidence; the character can choose a new subject/medium/structure
   without compulsory repeated lore motifs or fallback recipes.
6. Operator corrections are attributed events with explicit authority and
   effects. They do not rewrite original encounter or trait-history receipts.

## Verification

Red identity/binding, slow-change, contradiction, cross-facet conflict and
restart/pruning cases. Paired scenarios demonstrate an evidence-supported
preference affecting a choice; inspect the actual selected memories and state.

## Risks

Credential identity mistaken for character identity, false personality claims,
unsupported trait inference, commitment loss and self-reinforcing taste collapse.

## Context

Existing successful creations, vector hits, graph metadata, candidate images and
HTTP health do not verify the complete character loop. The active maker must
keep working during review and preparation. Deployment needs the existing
reserved head, terminal ownership/fencing, publication and lifecycle guarantees.

## Outcome

A reproducible verification path proves the entire loop on qualified revisions,
then a bounded live sequence demonstrates the same causal relationships and
independently observed outcomes with one event consumer owner.

## Scope

Cross-repository revision-bound fixtures and human runnable verification,
deployment/rollback proof for affected services/contracts, and natural clock
observation. Keep original identity, timestamps, images, contract hashes,
seeds, artifact hashes, graph paths and publication/outcome IDs inspectable.

## Non-goals

Complete the epic with a small vector/transport test, claim novelty from changed
adjectives, reset history, restart active makers, move cloud event ownership, or
waive native Rheos/canonical review and production qualification.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Isolated scenarios prove each full link: admitted outside event -> physical
   graph/field update -> separate mood/attention -> authorized traced recall ->
   creative/social choice -> verified outcome -> memory/relationship update.
2. Under fixed seed/config, paired different encounters change an actual
   association and choice. Replay with identical input recovers the same state
   and trace within declared tolerance. Missing links explicitly fail.
3. Restart, concurrent facets, delayed/out-of-order observations, denied memory,
   graph/appraisal failure, unknown social effects and context pruning retain
   truthful state and immutable provenance. Failed effects do not count as work.
4. While maker/intake/graph/appraisal lanes are saturated, the reserved head
   acknowledges and none of the held maker identities is aborted or replaced.
   Terminal parent/delegate/effect ownership is proven before recovery.
5. Exact tested candidate revisions, current personal review/base bindings,
   native lawful predecessor readiness and independent deployment gates all
   pass before affected production services/contracts are changed. Candidate
   readiness does not enable a second clock/gateway consumer.
6. After qualified idle/fenced deployment, natural clock opportunities show
   changing outside context, recalled association and choice; saved artifacts
   and actual social/destination results are independently inspected. Report
   quality/variety limits separately from transport and tool completion.

## Verification

The script verifies served revisions and credentials/scope prerequisites first,
creates and cleans only owned isolated fixtures, exits nonzero for broken links,
and names explicit warnings for unverified availability/quality. Live observation
never replays an existing post or interrupts a maker. Completion requires the
whole epic audit, not a locally passing subset.

## Risks

Different repositories serving different revisions, unqualified parent review,
missing native dependency admission, flaky remote APIs and artistic claims that
automated causal tests cannot establish alone.

tasks.content:
## Context

The maker is dominated by repeated production tasks and its own outputs. Knoxx
already has feed, notification and thread adapters; the live maker's tools do
not currently expose that discovery loop. Outside material must become durable
observations with real source identity, rather than ambient prompt authority.

## Outcome

A bounded intake facet continuously supplies actual changing encounters between
creative clock opportunities. The graph retains people, topics, replies and
sources with original identities, observation times and visibility.

## Scope

Authenticated home feed, replies/mentions, selected follows and a configured
small external-source set through existing adapters. Persist cursors, external
IDs and content hashes through existing event/memory stores; retain author and
relationship links. Intake is cheaper than a maker turn and does not require
publication or a model call for every item.

## Non-goals

Scrape arbitrary private content, infer read sources from output destinations,
invent encounters, echo every self-post as fresh outside novelty, introduce a
second gateway owner, or replace the native creative clock.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The same external item across pagination, retry, reconnect and two facets is
   admitted once by its canonical external identity. Changed content is a new
   attributed revision, not a silent rewrite of historical evidence.
2. A successful cursor is durable; interrupted batches resume without missing
   or duplicating admitted observations. Empty, malformed, failed and partial
   feeds remain distinguishable and cannot advance a failed page's cursor.
3. Self-output, outside authors, replies and explicit operator input retain
   separate provenance. Source/account/visibility/actual UTC observation time
   and author/topic relationships reach the existing graph projection.
4. A configured exploration budget admits a changing source beyond current
   interests, with its selection seed/reason recorded. Repeated own output alone
   cannot satisfy the outside-input test.
5. External text cannot alter permissions, model routing or effect admission.
   Intake queues, per-source requests, bytes and retention have explicit bounds.
6. The fifteen-minute maker reads changed admitted state without intake creating
   a second creative timer, clock owner or unbounded LLM invocation stream.

## Verification

Red adapter fixtures cover duplicate IDs, edits, pagination, disconnect/retry,
self-posts, invalid content and private-source denial. Observe capture and graph
projection separately. A later live read records actual cursors and source IDs
without replaying posts or exposing tokens/content from private sources.

## Risks

API pagination drift, source outages, stale deleted content, bot feedback,
sensitive graph context and starvation of quieter sources.

## Context

Native CodeRabbit review `5442414707`, finding `4206988928`, identifies an
unassigned kernel/numeric choice ahead of the 8-point physical-field story.
Fork Tales supplies experimental Python mechanics and later corrections;
OpenPlanner supplies current graph persistence/query seams, and Foresight favors
portable laws where practical. Those facts do not decide the owning library or
numeric contract by themselves.

## Outcome

A reviewed, revision-bound architecture decision names one owning kernel and
its numeric/replay contract before solver implementation begins. It is an
explicit proposed predecessor of `ff3e628b-cd5c-4a89-a397-42cc88dbde70`.

## Scope

The current Foresight coordinator owns recovering the source-to-law mapping and
publishing the selection for planning review. The decision must name the owning
repository, library/module and integration seams, then be acknowledged through
that repository's reviewed implementation plan. OpenPlanner retains ownership
of its persistence/query surface; Knoxx retains product integration. A shared
law promotion needs its own reviewed authority decision.

Initial Markdown is proposed input. Native Rheos retention/enforcement of the
predecessor edge must be delivered and verified through the epic's separately
owned upstream prerequisite before either story is admitted.

## Non-goals

Implement a solver before selection, assign common-law authority from a donor
name, duplicate a graph force engine, copy Fork Tales' effect runtime, migrate
board semantics locally, or treat a documentation link as native admission.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The decision names one owning repository and library/module, accountable
   implementation role, consumer adapters and exact reviewed source revisions.
   It explains which Fork Tales corrections are retained and any non-equivalent
   older formulation. Unresolved mechanics stay blocking rather than disappearing
   from the solver's acceptance criteria.
2. It specifies numeric representation on each actual target, units, timestep
   schedule and bounds, finite-value behavior, seeded exploration semantics,
   rounding/order rules and declared absolute/relative replay tolerances.
   Cross-runtime parity is required only for targets the decision actually selects.
3. It maps solver state, graph/field persistence and traced recall to their
   ownership boundaries, including authorization before traversal and feedback.
   There is one physical computation authority with outward runtime adapters.
4. Independent planning review assesses the choice and its estimates. Native
   Rheos records lawful readiness and the retained predecessor relationship
   after the upstream admission prerequisite passes. Before that, the relationship
   and 3-point estimate remain provisional.
5. The successor's RED tests and GREEN solver/replay bind this decision's revision,
   kernel configuration and numeric tolerance; a changed selection requires fresh
   review and cannot reuse incompatible replay evidence.

## Verification

Retain the decision diff, source map, native review IDs and exact source/kernel
revisions. Use native Rheos for readiness and predecessor observations. The
successor demonstrates executable numeric and coupling laws after admission;
static planning checks do not prove that the solver exists or replays correctly.

## Risks

Premature common-law promotion, a choice incompatible with persistence or host
targets, numeric tolerance hiding divergent behavior, and a nominal owner without
a reviewed owning-repository delivery plan. Three points is a planning estimate;
implementation cost remains in the separately reviewed solver story.

frontmatter.title: Select the physical graph kernel owner and numeric replay contract

tasks.content:
## Context

Served Knoxx hydrates memory using vector search and then session authorization.
The later API search was not a controlled reproduction of the maker. The current
scheduled maker records actor/role but no organization, membership or user; the
turn's synthesis adds no cross-session memory grant. Visibility rejects a
non-admin context lacking the required matching scope or grant. Graph retrieval
is a separate REST seam even when vectors use the direct Mongo client.

The [2026-10-07 source audit](../../notes/2026-10-07-cephalon-character-memory-graph.md#2026-10-07--bounded-hydration-source-audit)
binds these facts to S `2644fc6c51bbbcda599964a5a674415b58344c3b` and C
`366e72ab68c8afae708d3f6d5546faee808ebc07`, with source paths and immutable
line anchors. Search takes k before visibility and does not refill; the memory
event counts `:results` despite a `:hits` payload. The latter is an accounting
bug distinct from the eight actual persisted empty arrays. Detached indexing,
different API gates and the sessionless SDK fixture remain separate test inputs,
not an asserted historical cause or a new execution/installation claim.

## Outcome

A scheduled character obtains its authorized memories through graph-mediated
recall and includes useful traced context. Missing authority and unavailable
graph transport remain observable outcomes. An unrelated actor's private
memory stays inaccessible at seeds, traversal, returned context and feedback.

## Scope

Knoxx trusted event actor-context resolution, memory visibility decisions,
candidate/filter/inclusion diagnostics, bounded passive graph recall and existing
OpenPlanner graph seams. Resolve actual actor authority through the existing
identity/policy boundary; never infer grants from a display role. Review any
needed graph scope/feedback extension in OpenPlanner's personal fork.

Retain the [existing graph/projection boundary](../../notes/2026-10-07-cephalon-graph-recall-boundary.md)
and its separately pinned OpenPlanner observations: trail persistence flags do
not disable all feedback, selected reinforcement counts do not prove writes,
and scope must cover compacted views, trail/force influence and feedback before
they affect recall. The parent epic still requires the complete encounter ->
physical field -> independent mood -> graph recall -> choice -> observed outcome
loop, including physical replay, continuity and social obligations.

## Non-goals

Make context nil or administrator to bypass filtering, grant arbitrary
cross-session access, accept payload-chosen credentials, replace vector storage,
call a feedback-writing query a pure read, or require an LLM for this fixture.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Freeze query, corpus and authenticated maker principal. The prior path fails
   to include an authorized stored encounter; the repaired path includes it.
   Retain candidate IDs, exclusion reasons and included IDs with visibility-safe
   operator diagnostics. State the proven cause separately from historical clues.
   Include the bounded k=6/fetch-18 case with six denied leading candidates and
   an authorized seventh candidate after quality ordering. Preserve the search
   budget while preventing that candidate from being lost before visibility.
2. A scheduled actor obtains only its stored authorized scope through the
   existing resolver. Missing, revoked and mismatched bindings fail closed;
   a payload cannot choose a role, organization or permission grant.
3. Scope is enforced before graph expansion and reinforcement. A private node,
   connecting edge or hidden intermediate cannot leak through path text, scores,
   metadata or persisted trails. Public and explicitly shared memories obey
   their actual admission policy, not an invented role-based exception.
   Hidden nodes/edges, compacted members, trails and forces cannot causally alter
   authorized ranking, path selection or feedback even when their text is omitted.
4. Recall includes a memory reached through an authorized graph edge beyond the
   semantic seed, with node IDs, traversal path, reasons, graph/field revision
   and explicit inclusion budget. A vector-only result cannot satisfy this case.
   Inspect the actual assembled prompt: the authorized encounter and traversal
   context must reach the scheduled character, not only a returned result map.
5. Empty authorized corpus, denied candidates, indexing delay, transport error,
   timeout and budget exhaustion are distinct results. A failed graph path does
   not silently become a successful empty recall.
6. Duplicate recall cannot multiply reinforcement; unadmitted retrieval cannot
   reinforce hidden nodes. Deliberate feedback is attributed to this recall.
7. Existing legacy request contexts and privacy negatives retain behavior. The
   conversation head uses a bounded shared snapshot outside its acknowledgment
   path; heavy recall cannot consume the reserved head lane.
8. Memory event counts use the memory hit payload and agree with its persisted
   hit count. Report actual prompt inclusion separately when its budget reduces
   context; candidate, authorized-hit and included-hit counts need not be equal.
   Distinguish raw candidates, quality survivors, authorized hits and included
   hits. Feedback distinguishes attempted, completed, partial and failed writes;
   a selected-operation count or HTTP 200 cannot attest completed persistence.

## Verification

Red tests use the actual automatic and tool/API adapters with identical corpus
and principal, held provider boundaries and real graph result shapes. Include
negative authority and hidden-path cases, a graph-neighbor inclusion case and
transport failures. Run the relevant Knoxx and OpenPlanner gates separately;
bind proofs to both revisions. A live passive turn is observed only after
qualified deployment; do not invoke the active maker to prepare fixtures.

The following are prospective RED scenarios; none was authored or executed by
the static audit or this planning update. Use the source revisions/paths in the
linked audit and retain fixture query, corpus/index snapshot, candidate IDs and
order, quality labels, principal/grants, limits and selected transport.

- **Authorized lower candidate:** feed the real search/visibility adapters the
  same frozen nested vector result with six quality-eligible denied candidates
  before an authorized seventh, k=6 and fetch-18. The predecessor loses the
  authorized candidate; the acceptance test requires bounded inclusion without
  admitting the denied leading candidates or silently broadening permissions.
- **Matched inputs and endpoint gates:** compare automatic hydration and the
  memory tool/API with the full stored query, candidate set, options and trusted
  principal held fixed. Verify API memory-read and cross-session gates explicitly;
  a correct route refusal need not equal passive hydration's result. Do not add
  a grant, nil context or admin role solely to force endpoint parity.
- **Strict denial and decoding:** missing/revoked/ambiguous/mismatched bindings,
  foreign/private sessions, session-fetch rejection and missing session metadata
  remain denied. Keep legacy policy controls explicit. Supply a separate positive
  nested-array fixture with session metadata and matching stored ownership rows;
  the current canned SDK hit/session lookup cannot serve as that positive proof.
- **Graph scope and causal isolation:** include an authorized neighbor beyond
  the seed, then vary only hidden connecting nodes/edges, compacted members and
  trail/force samples under a fixed seed/config/scope snapshot. Authorized paths,
  rankings, prompt context and feedback must not change because of denied data.
  Enforce scope before expansion/projection influence and writes, not afterward.
- **Transport and readiness:** hold vector and REST graph boundaries separately.
  Local Mongo vector success with unavailable/failed/timed-out graph transport
  must remain an explicit graph failure. Hold detached indexing completion apart
  from event acceptance; freeze candidates before/after fixture readiness and
  never infer earlier availability from a later API result.
- **Telemetry and prompt inclusion:** exercise the actual turn assembly and
  publication boundary with positive authorized memory and a graph path. Require
  the event's memory count to match the `:hits` payload, preserve the resource
  array, and inspect the prompt actually passed onward. Empty/denied/failure and
  inclusion-budget cases must keep their distinct counts and outcomes.
- **Deliberate feedback:** replay one stable recall/effect identity and inject
  partial/failed writes. Verify no duplicate or unauthorized reinforcement,
  truthful persistence outcomes and explicit consumer compatibility. A trail-off
  flag or successful retrieval response alone cannot establish no effects.

Reuse the existing C hydration outage, semantic nested-result/request, SDK
conversion, hydration-publication and actor-membership fixture seams listed in
the audit. Their current coverage is not a positive authorized graph recall
proof. Graph boundary observations remain isolated synthetic I/O evidence;
upstream integration and each owning implementation's qualification are separate.

## Risks

Existing actor contexts may omit organization on purpose; repair requires actual
stored authority rather than guessed grants. Current graph-memory reinforces
edges and persists trails; output filtering after those writes is insufficient.
Scope-aware expansion may require an independently reviewed OpenPlanner change.

## Context

The human explicitly included this narrow two-point prerequisite in the current
character milestone on 2026-10-14: “Include the narrow canonical repair.”
The owning issue is https://github.com/riatzukiza/.agents/issues/25.
ETA PR15 has current approving reviews and passing deterministic checks but the
canonical withdrawal predicate requires its original finding's immutable review
commit to equal the latest PR head. A later opener recheck cannot mutate that
original review. The original native root and history must remain inspectable.

## Outcome

A configured native finding opener can withdraw its own older finding after a
current-head recheck; a subsequent authorized current-head writer settlement
can clear that finding through the canonical law. Original severity, root,
review identity and source commit remain preserved.

## Scope

Owning `.agents` pure PR-flow withdrawal predicate, regression fixtures, skill/contract wording and protected adoption. Collector/acquisition/pagination/identity-custody changes are excluded: the actual existing collector already captures original and current enclosing reviews and complete native conversation. If this pure repair proves insufficient, stop and report the owning gap for a separately scoped and estimated prerequisite before changing collector code.
The Foresight card is the primary board artifact. The owning source PR carries
an explicitly attributed planning snapshot, not another board implementation.
Keep the existing two-point estimate for this included prerequisite.

## Non-goals

Change approval or cohort policy, waive checks, add native identities, create a
local classifier, accept copied Bot transcripts or general cross-thread agreement,
rewrite receipts, add repository fields, change credentials/models/paid usage,
or change character runtime, clock, gateway, grants or publication.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Freeze the actual old-root conversation and immutable review commit. A
   clearly labeled prospective fixture with a current native opener withdrawal
   and later current authorized writer reproduces the false refusal before the
   change. Original raw bytes remain distinct from fixture-only mutations.
2. Preserve the original root/review/commit and conservative severity. Admit a
   known older original commit only when the actual current-head configured
   opener withdrawal and subsequent writer match repository/PR/thread/root,
   complete ordered native context, substantive rationale/evidence and chronology.
3. Stale withdrawal or writer, missing/malformed original binding, wrong opener,
   repository/PR/root, partial pagination, unresolved/outdated conversation,
   unknown timestamps, later edits/retraction/pushback and nonwriter identity
   remain denied. Unknown history never becomes an empty successful history.
4. Existing same-head withdrawal, rejection, native body/thread obligations,
   approval/full-input/cohort/required-check and merge-head guards retain behavior.
   The new disposition grants no approval, review round, quota or CI credit.
5. Run all owning PR-flow laws, policy, CLI, portable and lint gates. Complete
   current-head planning/code review and protected history-preserving MERGE.
   Only then adopt the reviewed source and obtain fresh native withdrawal/writer
   evidence on ETA PR15; historical752 evidence cannot qualify current564.

6. Before this prerequisite is admitted Ready, reconcile its parent epic through
   qualified Rheos: add this child UUID/two-point scope to the native inventory,
   and apply the independently reviewed enumerated total of 39 points
   (the existing proposed37 plus this included2). Read back the actual epic
   UUID/type, points and scope comment. Preserve prior34/37 source and events;
   the arithmetic is a proposal until planning review qualifies it. No readiness
   may rely only on the old Incoming34 readback or a duplicated source snapshot.

## Verification

Planning review assesses this scope, two-point estimate, identities/bindings and
negative matrix before lawful Rheos readiness. RED/GREEN follows readiness.
Use the actual native ETA conversation plus explicit fixture-only current-head
successors, preserving every original byte and ledger prefix. Capture exact
commands/results, full changed input and final merged/adopted source hashes.
Current application/deployment and B1/B2/B3 behavior are separate later evidence.

## Risks

Confusing old root provenance with stale current authority; weakening native
chronology or trusting partial capture; accepting withdrawn rejection agreement
as finding withdrawal; masking later conflicts; tests depending on unavailable
provider or live network. Keep source qualification and actual adoption separate.
